A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DefCon research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on FMNIST and UTKFACE, including individual defenses, 30 pairwise combinations, and three-defense combinations in Tables 4, 6, and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains original defense-combination experiments, revises robustness results, and adds hyperparameter-tuning outcomes in Section 7.4 and qualitative CENSUS results in Section 8.

M1.justification: The pairwise S1–S4 rules remain unchanged. However, v1's incremental procedure checks each additional defense against existing defenses, whereas v2 Section 5.3 introduces stagewise permutation search, pruning of conflicting orders, and composition of stage-specific defense sequences. This substantially revises the multi-defense procedure.

E1.justification: FMNIST and UTKFACE coverage remains unchanged. v2 Section 8 adds a limited CENSUS tabular-data evaluation: robustness plus explanations and fairness plus explanations reportedly match DefCon's predictions. This extends modality coverage, although only qualitative outcomes are supplied.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator remains naïve mutually exclusive placement, renamed from A2 to T2. Corresponding experiments retain the same constituent defenses and no-defense/single-defense references. The revised adversarial attacks change evaluation procedures, not the comparator against DefCon.

E3.justification: v1 Section 6.3 evaluates robustness with 40-step PGD. v2 Section 6.4 uses optimized AutoAttack variants with CE/DLR losses, expectation over transformations, and random starts, reporting the lowest robust accuracy. Section 7.4 also introduces grid-search protocols for eight conflicting combinations. The principal image datasets, splits, and architectures are retained.

E4.justification: v1 leaves hyperparameter tuning as future work. v2 Section 7.4 systematically tests whether tuning resolves three false positives or overturns five correctly predicted conflicts. It reports resolution of C32 and a dataset-specific resolution of C23, substantially expanding sensitivity analysis beyond the earlier speculative failure explanations.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across five runs and retain the fingerprinting p-value threshold and data-watermarking t-test. Additional tuning outcomes use the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Robustness results are substantially replaced under the revised protocol: individual-defense UTKFACE robust accuracy changes from 68.45 ± 1.25 in v1 Table 4 to 37.38 ± 1.30 in v2 Table 3, and C35 changes from 49.28 ± 3.31 to 0.00 ± 0.00. These are not same-setting performance comparisons. v2 also adds tuning outcomes and reports 86% balanced accuracy after tuning, while retaining 81% before tuning.

T1.justification: New Appendices B–C introduce defense tuples, pairwise and multi-way classification functions, consistency and coverage proofs, and conditional soundness/completeness analyses. v1 has no corresponding formal analysis. The addition is substantive, although Appendix B's same-stage conflict condition differs from the retained main-text S2 rule.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the reported empirical headline from 81% to 86% accuracy on 30 combinations, reflecting the new tuning results. The 90% result on eight prior-work combinations and the central claims of accuracy, scalability, non-invasiveness, and generality remain.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's argument that ten omitted in-training combinations would be ineffective with an explicit statement that their evaluation remains future work. Sections 7.4–8 add substantive qualifications: unsuccessful tuning does not prove fundamental incompatibility, conflict causes may be incomplete, validation is laboratory-based, and binary predictions omit application-dependent trade-offs.

D1.justification: v2 provides a code-repository link where v1 only promises release, and adds attack implementation details, pruning thresholds, and the tuning ranges in Table 6. Conversely, v1's explicit perturbation budget and TRADES step settings disappear. These are documentation and access changes; the PDFs do not establish that every newly disclosed setting changed.

R1.justification: The largely retained survey adds robustness-evaluation literature, including Croce and Hein, Carlini et al., and Pintor et al., while revising some classifications and positioning. For example, Thakkar et al.'s combination changes from optimization plus placement in v1 to placement alone in v2. The central relationship to mutually exclusive placement remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized around a systematization framework, survey, and derived insights. Defense descriptions are split between Sections 3 and 6, terminology is globally renamed, and the abstract, introduction, and discussion are substantially revised. These changes exceed the prose needed merely to insert new experiments.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes predominantly single-column with wrapped tables and takeaway boxes. The defense-parameter table is transposed, the defense inventory moves to Appendix A, the notation glossary is removed, and a hyperparameter table is added. Figure 1 is redrawn while preserving its pairwise logic, and retained result tables are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through optimized attacks, an actual tuning study replacing speculation, and clearer limitations. These benefits are tempered by new inconsistencies: Appendix B's conflict rule differs from Section 5.3, and Table 5 keeps C12 green although FMNIST explanation error rises from 0.12 ± 0.03 to 0.22 ± 0.01 against an unchanged baseline. The stronger evaluation provides a limited net improvement, but these issues weaken confidence in the added formal support and headline accuracy.
